Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Ventura CTO), Lena (Head of ML), Mark (Infra Ops), Holly (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intros - I'm Jordan, AE on the account, and I'm joined by Priya and Evan from our SE team.
[00:08] Carlos: Hey Jordan thanks, Carlos here. Quick note we've got about 45 minutes, thanks.
[00:12] Jordan: Great, objective for today is to understand your workload and see if Redwood Dedicated is the right fit vs hosted or private. We'll cover GPUs/reserved capacity, isolation needs, burst strategy and scaling expectations.
[00:24] Lena: Yep, that's exactly it. We run a set of customer-facing LLM features - conversational support, document understanding, and risk detection models. Latency matters for some flows and security/regulatory controls for others.
[00:36] Priya: Could you give us traffic patterns - avg qps, peak windows, types of models? even ballpark is fine.
[00:42] Lena: Sure. For chat: baseline is roughly 20 qps across all users, peaks around 120 qps during market open 9:30-10:00 and again 16:00. Embeddings batch jobs run nightly - approx 2M docs per day but can be batched. Model wise we use a mix of open Llama-like and a few larger 70B variants for summaries and detection.
[01:03] Evan: Got it - are the 70B runs low-latency or offline?
[01:08] Lena: Mostly async for heavy inference, but we'd also like a lower-latency 70B path for escalations, maybe 3-5 second P50.
[01:15] Mark: To add, infra is in AWS, we use EKS with private subnets. We have strict egress rules and require VPC peering for any provider.
[01:24] Holly: From security perspective we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[01:34] Jordan: That's helpful. On Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools in your tenancy with VPC peering or private-link connectivity for the Private control plane option. For on-prem we also support air-gapped installs but most banks do VPC peering.
[01:48] Carlos: Can you clarify isolation? We need ensured data separation and dedicated GPUs not shared with other customers.
[01:55] Priya: Yes - Dedicated means dedicated capacity: reserved GPU nodes only for your org. Compute isolation is physical (customer-dedicated nodes) and we can also restrict image access and IAM roles. For extra controls we offer Private deploy where control plane sits in your VPC.
[02:12] Mark: And in that Private control plane model, do we still see Redwood-managed updates or do we take ownership?
[02:18] Evan: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane variant where updates can be staged - Redwood still provides tooling and patches but we can support you to validate updates in your environment. There's an enterprise ops agreement around that.
[02:31] Lena: Great. Burst capacity - how do you handle spikes from 20 to 120 qps quickly? Autoscale? Pre-warm?
[02:38] Priya: We support a few patterns: reserved baseline capacity + burst buckets on demand (if you allow a shared capacity fallback) or reserved nodes + fast vertical scaling via warm standby nodes. For strict isolation, burst is done via reserved burst pool that's dedicated to you; it requires commit for sizing but still cheaper than over-provisioning full time.
[02:56] Jordan: Another option is hybrid: baseline Dedicated and allow controlled fallback to Hosted during rare spikes with encryption and routing policies. But that requires contractual protections and is less common for regulated banks.
[03:09] Carlos: We probably can't risk fallback to multi-tenant hosted for PII-sensitive traffic. Might consider fallback for anonymized/low-risk flows.
[03:17] Holly: Exactly - any fallback must be opt-in and not carry customer PII.
[03:22] Mark: What's the lead time to add GPUs? If we commit to a baseline of 8 A100-like GPUs, and need to double during quarter end, how fast can you add?
[03:31] Priya: Typical provisioning for Dedicated in Redwood's hosted model is a few hours once capacity in region is available, but reserved capacity contracts ensure capacity availability. If you need guaranteed rapid scaling, reserved burst capacity is committed and available immediately. For Private/on-prem installs lead times are longer - hardware procurement applies.
[03:47] Lena: Do you have benchmarks for throughput and latency per GPU for the 70B models? We want concrete numbers.
[03:54] Evan: We'll share our verified performance profiles in the post-call pack; as a rule of thumb a 70B quantized to 4-bit on A100 does X tokens/sec - we'll include token-per-second and cost per token for your expected prompt lengths. Also we suggest running a SE-led benchmark with your exact prompts to get apples-to-apples.
[04:13] Carlos: Good, please do that. We also have internal models that use KV cache heavy prompting - how does Redwood handle KV cache warmups and session affinity?
[04:20] Priya: Our serving runtime manages KV cache and supports sticky sessions to keep caches hot. For heavy stateful workloads we recommend pinning to nodes or pre-warmed KV cache strategies. Apologies if I said K V cash earlier in internal docs, transcription sometimes funny.
[04:36] Lena: (laughs) heard that.
[04:38] Holly: On compliance - can you enumerate artifacts: SOC2 report, penetration test summaries, data flow diagrams, and KMS integration docs? We need to present to our auditors.
[04:48] Jordan: Yes - we'll share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and a network architecture diagram showing VPC peering and private endpoints. For KMS we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via AWS KMS/HSM integrations.
[05:01] Carlos: Any certification around data residency? We need EU and US separation for certain customers.
[05:06] Jordan: We support region pinning and data residency controls; we can advise on deploying Dedicated in specific cloud regions or via Private for stricter geo controls.
[05:14] Mark: Ok, pricing - ballpark for reserved GPUs? Our finance wants an idea for 8-16 GPUs committed.
[05:21] Jordan: I'll send a dedicated pricing grid after this call - depends on GPU class and commitment term. We do monthly and annual reserved pricing with burst pool addons.
[05:30] Lena: Timeline - we're aiming for a Q3 pilot with a small set of customers. What would you recommend as pilot scope?
[05:36] Priya: Start with two routes: one low-latency chat flow on a smaller 13B/30B model and one async heavy workload on the 70B quantized path. Run 2-4 weeks of benchmarks including latency P50/P95 and throughput. That gives you a safety margin before scaling to prod.
[05:49] Evan: We'll need sample prompts, typical sequence lengths, and an ops contact for peering and firewall rules.
[05:55] Mark: I'll share VPC CIDRs, security groups, and the egress policy.
[05:59] Carlos: Who will run the benchmark - you or us?
[06:02] Priya: SE-led with your participation - Redwood runs tests in a controlled environment using your prompts and we provide raw logs and a summary report.
[06:10] Holly: Any retention policies? We need 90-day logs and the ability to purge model inputs on request.
[06:16] Jordan: We support configurable retention, and for Dedicated/Private you control retention policy; we can implement end-to-end deletion workflows for compliance.
[06:25] Lena: Are eval/regression monitoring features part of the offering? We want quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[06:31] Evan: Yes - Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks and regression alerts; we can integrate that into the Dedicated instance for continuous monitoring.
[06:38] Carlos: Ok, last quick questions: SLA for latency and uptime on Dedicated?
[06:43] Jordan: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated (99.9%+) and latency SLOs vary by model class; we'll surface current measured SLOs in the follow-up.
[06:51] Lena: Sounds good.
[06:52] Jordan: Wrap-up recap: we'll send pricing & sizing, SOC2 and network diagrams, and a proposed benchmark plan. SEs will schedule the deep-dive next week. Any other blockers?
[07:04] Mark: None from infra. I'll share peering details.
[07:07] Holly: I'll review the SOC2 docs when you send them.
[07:10] Carlos: Thanks everyone, look forward to the benchmark.
[07:13] Jordan: Thanks all - talk soon.
